title: 18+ Meetings With Airline and MRO Operations Leaders for an AI Platform
summary: An AI operations platform needed a way into airline and MRO operations teams.
metaDescription: Case study: 18+ meetings booked with airline and MRO operations leaders for an AI operations platform through research-led outbound.
reached: Ops directors and heads of maintenance at US operators
role: Research, targeting, outreach and meeting booking
challenge: A complex buying process and hard-to-find decision-makers meant generic outreach to aviation operators went unanswered.
context: The client sells AI-driven fleet, scheduling and maintenance dashboards. The buyers are operations directors and heads of maintenance at US airlines and MRO providers, people with crowded inboxes and a long, multi-stakeholder evaluation process.
responsibility: I handled the research, account targeting, outreach and meeting booking. The client's sales team ran the calls and the evaluation that followed.
significance: Eighteen scheduled conversations with operations leaders gave the client direct access to a market that had ignored generic outreach. These are meetings, not closed deals, and no revenue is claimed for this engagement.
takeaway: In a market with few buyers and long evaluations, a narrow, well-researched list beats a broad one. The first message only has to earn a reply from the right person.
photoAlt: Aircraft parked on an airport apron at sunset

title: Opening Corporate Travel Conversations for a Private Charter Operator
summary: A charter operator selling flights, not software, needed business buyers to ask for a quote.
metaDescription: Case study: research-led outreach that opened corporate travel conversations for a private charter operator selling flights and block-hour packages.
sells: Charter flights and flexible block-hour packages
reached: Corporate travel managers and executive assistants
role: Account research, outreach and enquiry handoff to sales
challenge: Charter was seen as a last-minute luxury. Buyers needed a clear business case before they would ask for a quote.
context: Unlike the technology cases, this client is an industry company selling its own service. The goal was not a software demo but a quote request from a corporate travel decision-maker.
responsibility: I researched the best-fit accounts, ran the outreach and passed warm enquiries to the client's sales team. Quoting and booking sat with the client.
significance: This engagement shows the second way I work: selling for an industry company rather than into an industry. The aim was to turn a luxury perception into a business conversation. Result figures for this engagement are shared on a call.
takeaway: When the product has a reputation problem, the first message should reframe the purchase as a business decision before it asks for any commitment.
photoAlt: Private jets parked on an airport apron

title: 25+ Qualified Conversations to Take a Healthcare Software Platform to Market
summary: A patient-management platform replaced broad, product-first messaging with relevance-led outreach.
metaDescription: Case study: 25+ qualified conversations with clinic and hospital leaders for a healthcare software platform with EMR integrations.
reached: Practice owners, COOs and clinical IT leads
role: ICP definition, personalised outreach and call booking
challenge: Broad targeting and product-first messaging created low-trust conversations with busy healthcare leaders.
context: The client offers a patient-management platform that connects with existing EMR systems. Healthcare buyers are cautious, time-poor and quick to dismiss anything that reads like a generic software pitch.
responsibility: I defined the ideal customer profile, wrote the personalised outreach and booked the calls. The client's team handled demos and any follow-on conversations.
significance: Twenty-five qualified conversations with practice and clinical leaders gave the client a real read on where the platform fit. The 2.6x response rate points to relevance doing more work than volume. These are conversations, not signed contracts.
takeaway: In healthcare, trust is the bottleneck. Messaging that shows you understand the practice's workflow earns the conversation that a feature list never will.
photoAlt: A doctor reviewing documents with a colleague in a clinic

title: A Steady Qualified Pipeline for a B2B SaaS Platform Through Research-Led Outreach
summary: A growth-stage SaaS company moved from volume-led outreach to a research-led engine.
metaDescription: Case study: 40+ qualified conversations and 3.2x more qualified replies for a B2B SaaS platform through research-led LinkedIn and email outreach.
reached: Heads of operations and revenue at mid-market firms
role: Research, LinkedIn and email sequences, CRM tracking
challenge: Unclear target buyers, low engagement and an inconsistent pipeline limited the platform's visibility.
context: The client sells workflow automation and analytics to mid-market operations and revenue teams. Outreach had been volume-focused, which produced activity but not a dependable flow of qualified replies.
responsibility: I ran the research, built the LinkedIn and email sequences and tracked every conversation in the CRM so the client could see pipeline movement.
significance: Forty-plus qualified conversations and 3.2x more qualified replies show a repeatable engine rather than a one-off spike. The figures describe conversations and replies, not closed revenue.
takeaway: A consistent pipeline comes from knowing who should hear from you, not from sending more messages to everyone.

title: Opening Proposal Conversations for an IT Services Firm Selling Custom Software
summary: An IT services firm needed founders and CTOs to answer when they hear from dozens of agencies each week.
metaDescription: Case study: research-led outreach to founders and CTOs for a software development and IT consulting firm selling MVPs, custom software and AI integrations.
client: Software development and IT consulting firm
sells: MVPs, custom software and AI integrations
reached: Founders and CTOs at funded US startups
role: Market research, outreach and solution-fit assessment
challenge: Founders get dozens of agency pitches a week. Without a specific reason to talk, outreach was deleted.
context: This client is a services firm selling its own build capacity. Its buyers are founders and CTOs who have heard every agency pitch and need a concrete reason to reply.
responsibility: I researched target startups, wrote the outreach and assessed solution fit, whether a prospect needed an MVP, a full build, an AI integration or a dashboard, before handing the conversation to the client.
significance: The point of this engagement was relevance: each message gave a founder a specific reason to talk. Result figures for this engagement are shared on a call.
takeaway: Agency outreach fails when it describes the agency. It works when it describes the prospect's next problem.
photoAlt: Lines of code on a dark screen

title: 15+ Sales Opportunities Created With Global Supply Chain Leaders for a Logistics Technology Vendor
summary: A fragmented global market and many decision-makers made logistics buyers hard to reach.
metaDescription: Case study: 40+ qualified conversations and 15+ sales opportunities with supply chain leaders for a logistics technology vendor.
sells: Shipment tracking and warehouse management software
reached: VPs of logistics and supply chain operations
role: Account mapping, decision-maker research and outreach
challenge: A fragmented global market and multiple decision-makers made logistics buyers hard to reach with generic outreach.
context: The client sells shipment tracking and warehouse management software. Buying decisions involve several people across logistics, operations and IT, and the target market is spread across many regions.
responsibility: I mapped the accounts, identified the right decision-makers inside each one and ran the outreach. Opportunity qualification was shared with the client's sales team.
significance: Forty-plus qualified conversations turned into 15+ sales opportunities, so the engagement reached beyond first replies into real pipeline. Opportunities are not closed deals and no revenue is claimed.
takeaway: Complex buying groups need account mapping first. Knowing who sits on the decision before writing a word saves the whole sequence.

title: 20+ Qualified Conversations With Finance Leaders for a Fintech Product
summary: Finance leaders ignored generic outreach, so the work started with who they are and what they own.
metaDescription: Case study: 20+ qualified conversations and 8+ sales opportunities with CFOs and finance directors for a fintech software company.
role: ICP definition, outreach and pipeline tracking
service: ICP definition, outreach and pipeline tracking
challenge: Complex buying decisions and hard-to-reach finance leaders meant generic outreach was consistently ignored.
context: The client sells finance operations and reporting tools. Its buyers are CFOs, controllers and finance directors, a group that gets heavy vendor traffic and expects a clear business reason before replying.
responsibility: I defined the ICP, ran the outreach and kept the pipeline organised in the CRM. Commercial conversations after qualification sat with the client.
significance: Twenty-plus qualified conversations and 8+ sales opportunities show that relevant research reached a hard audience. These are pipeline stages, not revenue.

title: A 3x Meeting Rate With Tax and Accounting Firms for an IT Automation Company
summary: Firms buried in manual bookkeeping still saw every automation pitch as one more tool to learn.

reached: Partners and finance leads at tax and accounting firms
role: ICP definition, personalised outreach and call booking
service: ICP definition and outbound meeting generation
challenge: Firms were buried in manual bookkeeping and spreadsheet reporting, but saw every automation pitch as one more tool to learn.
context: The client sells bookkeeping, reporting and compliance automation to tax and accounting firms. The firms feel the manual workload but are wary of adopting anything that adds to it.
responsibility: I defined the ICP, wrote the personalised outreach and booked the calls. The client's team led the conversations after booking.
